newsitem.title: UK: Virgin wins UK CrossCountry rail franchise.
newsitem.headline: Virgin wins UK CrossCountry rail franchise.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group confirmed on Friday it had clinched the CrossCountry passenger rail franchise under the government's privatisation of nationwide rail services.
Details of the deal including service levels and the government subsidy agreed with Virgin's rail arm will be announced at a press conference by the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising at 1200 GMT.
CrossCountry covers more than 100 stations and is headquartered in Birmingham. It has 842 staff and in the year to March 30 passenger revenues were 108 million pounds ($181.3 million).
The services run are branded InterCity or Express and link cities and destinations across England, Scotland and Wales.
This is the first rail franchise to be awarded to Virgin which also bid unsuccessfully for the Gatwick Express route which went to National Express buses.

The Virgin empire which spans everything from music to financial services and its own label Cola already has a major rail business - as partner in the UK Eurostar passenger service which runs through the Channel Tunnel, closed last week after a serious fire which has halted services.
